title: Session-affinity token deprecation & migration to stateless session header
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: We will deprecate the legacy session-affinity token header (X-Redwood-Session) that encoded sticky routing and server-side session state, and replace it with a lightweight, explicit stateless header (Redwood-Session-Id) that carries only an opaque client session id.

Background: The current X-Redwood-Session token contains server-side routing hints and encoded state which forces sticky placement of requests onto a particular backend pool. This complicates autoscaling, KV cache invalidation, and cross-model fallbacks. Several customers rely on its implicit behavior for conversational continuity. To improve routing flexibility, autoscaling elasticity, and make session lifecycle explicit for clients, we will phase out the legacy token and introduce a stateless header plus a migration adapter in SDKs and the API gateway.

Scope:
- Included: deprecation plan for X-Redwood-Session header, spec for Redwood-Session-Id header, SDK changes (Python/JS/Go) to emit the new header by default and support a compatibility mode, server-side gateway behavior to accept both headers during the transition, telemetry and QA gating, migration docs and CLI tooling for large customers, rollback criteria and canarying.
- Excluded: changes to Dedicated/private control plane (a follow-up ticket will cover on-prem upgrade packaging), deep changes to conversation persistence model, billing or quota model changes.

Goals:
1) Remove need for sticky placement for normal conversational workloads, enabling better batching and autoscaling.
2) Provide a clear migration path and tooling with minimal customer disruption.
3) Ensure we can detect regressions via telemetry and automatic rollback gates.

API changes and compatibility:
- New header: Redwood-Session-Id (string, opaque). Server will treat requests with Redwood-Session-Id as stateless routing keys; no sticky KV cache implied. Existing X-Redwood-Session will be honored in compatibility mode but will be logged and counted for deprecation telemetry.
- When both headers are present, Redwood-Session-Id takes precedence.
- A deprecation response header (X-Redwood-Deprecation-Info) will be sent for requests using X-Redwood-Session after the soft-deprecation date.

SDK behavior:
- SDKs will emit Redwood-Session-Id derived from existing session management APIs. A compatibility flag (legacySessionAffinity: true) will be available for customers who explicitly opt-in to preserve old behavior during migration windows.
- SDKs will include a CLI command (redwood migrate-sessions) to scan logs and surface customers still sending X-Redwood-Session tokens.

Telemetry and gating:
- Track request volume with X-Redwood-Session vs Redwood-Session-Id.
- Monitor per-customer error rates, latency P99, and KV-cache miss rate before/after switch.
- Rollout gates: hold migration if any customer experiences >10% increase in 99th percentile latency or >5% increase in error rate attributable to routing change.

Rollout timeline (high-level):
1) Soft-deprecation announcement & SDK beta: 2026-03-15 (announce public docs + SDK beta emitting new header).
2) Compatibility gateway and telemetry: 2026-04-01 (gateway accepts both headers, logs deprecation usage).
3) Migration window (customers): 2026-04-01 to 2026-07-01 (3 months): proactive outreach, CLI scanning, SDK nudges.
4) Soft enforcement: 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-01 (2 months) – requests with X-Redwood-Session will receive deprecation headers and reduced routing guarantees; compatibility flag still honored.
5) Hard enforcement / removal: 2026-09-01 – X-Redwood-Session no longer accepted on hosted API; private/dedicated customers will have individual schedules.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Out-of-scope risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Large customers with custom session behavior could see state loss. Mitigation: run early migrations with SEs, provide per-customer rollback channels and a one-click compatibility flag at gateway for enterprise accounts.
- Risk: SDKs introducing bugs. Mitigation: parallel SDK beta, cross-language smoke tests, nightly regression matrix that replays recorded sessions.

Documentation and comms:
- Detailed migration guide for engineers, step-by-step scripts, and sample server-side header translation snippets.
- Customer playbook for SEs with rollback procedures and telemetry dashboards.

Operational changes:
- Gateway teams to add logging, deprecation headers, and per-customer compatibility switch feature-flag.
- Console: new dashboard tile showing per-customer legacy header usage and recommended actions.

Acceptance signoffs required from: Product, API Platform Eng, SDK Leads, SRE/Observability, Security.
acceptance_criteria: All main SDKs (Python, JS, Go) default to emitting Redwood-Session-Id in beta by 2026-04-01 and provide a legacySessionAffinity compatibility flag
API gateway accepts both headers and emits X-Redwood-Deprecation-Info for legacy header use by 2026-04-01
Telemetry dashboard shows per-customer counts for legacy vs new header and alerts for any customer exceeding latency/error gates
Migration CLI scans historical logs and outputs a per-customer report with action items and runbook links
No critical customer reports of >10% P99 degradation attributable to header migration during the migration window
Rollout playbook and SE contingency channel are published and tested with 2 pilot customers before 2026-05-15
milestones: 2026-03-15: Public announcement + docs + SDK beta published
2026-04-01: Gateway compatibility + telemetry + console tile live
2026-05-15: Complete pilot migrations for two enterprise customers
2026-09-01: Target hard enforcement for hosted API
risks: Enterprise customers with in-memory app state tied to sticky routing may need code changes
SDK rollout could introduce regressions (regression matrix mitigates)
Private deployments may be delayed due to upgrade cadence — plan separate PKG ticket
